questions.question: If 9@3 = 12; 15@4 = 22; 16@14 = 4; then what is the value of 6@2 = ?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed is: (a - b) × 2

9@3 → (9 - 3) = 6 × 2 = 12

15@4 → (15 - 4) = 11 × 2 = 22

16@14 → (16 - 14) = 2 × 2 = 4

Similarly, 6@2 → (6 - 2) = 4 × 2 = 8

Hence, the correct answer is 8.

questions.question:
In a certain code language, '+' represents '×', '-' represents '+', '×' represents '÷' and '÷' represents '-'. What is the answer to the following question?

60 × 5 + 3 ÷ 24 - 6 = ?
questions.solution:
Refer to the table below:

 
 

 
 
**Symbol**

 
 
 
+

 
 
 
-

 
 
 
×

 
 
 
÷

 
 
 

 
 
**Code**

 
 
 
×

 
 
 
+

 
 
 
÷

 
 
 
-

 
 
 

 

Given: 60 × 5 + 3 ÷ 24 - 6 = ?

After converting the symbols with given code, the equation will be:

→ 60 ÷ 5 × 3 - 24 + 6 = ?

→ 12 × 3 - 24 + 6

→ 36 - 24 + 6

→ 42 - 24

→ 18

Hence, 18 is the answer

questions.question: Gurkiran's birthday is on Sunday 21st May. On what day of the week will be Shreyas's Birthday in the same year if Shreyas was born on 14th November?
questions.solution:
Gurkiran’s birthday is on 21st May on Sunday, so 10 days of May are remaining.

Therefore count rest of the days till the last date of that month as:

Remaining days of May → 10

June → 30

July → 31

August → 31

September → 30

October → 31

November → 14

Total days will be: 177

Now divide 177 by 7 (because 7 days in a week)

Remainder will be 2

Thus, 2 days after Sunday will be Tuesday.

Hence, Shreyas was born on Tuesday.

questions.question:
In the question a statement is given, followed by two arguments, I and II. You have to consider the statement to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given arguments, if any, is a strong argument.

**Statement:** Should mango export be banned to bring down domestic prices?

**Argument I:** Yes, environmentalists and dieticians too encourage eating only local fruits.

**Argument II:** No, exports bring in valuable foreign currency.

options.text: If only argument I is strong.
If only argument II is strong.
If both I and II are strong.
If neither I nor II is strong.

questions.solution:
For an argument to be strong, it should directly answer the statement problem.

Argument I is not strong because the opinion of environmentalists and dieticians won’t have any impact on the export of goods.

Argument II is strong because it explains that the impact on the export of goods will bring in valuable foreign currency by which it can be decided whether the export of mangoes should be banned or not.

Hence, only option 2 is correct.

questions.question: _________ scheme launched by the Central Government plans to issue soil cards to farmers which will carry crop-wise recommendations of nutrients and fertilisers.

questions.question: Indian Mughal paintings flourished during the rule of which Mughal Emperor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jahangir.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• During Jahangir's reign (1605-1627), Mughal Paintings reached its zenith.
 
• He took inspiration from his life events and pushed for paintings on those scenarios rather than illustrations on fiction.
 
• His themes were mostly secular.
 
• He encouraged portrait, scientific studies of birds, animals, and flowers collected in albums.
 
• His famous paintings include Mansur and Manohar. 
 
• But during the reign of Aurangzeb (1659-1707), Mughal Paintings started to decline.
 
• While the period of Muhammad Shah experienced a short revival of the Mughal Paintings, the onset of Shah Alam II almost made the art non-existent.
 
• As a result of artisans leaving Mughal emperor for the Rajput empire, the Rajput Paintings started developing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Akbar ruling period (1556-1605 AD) was known as a golden period for Mughals Administration.
 
• Shah Jahan ruling period (1628-1658 AD) was a golden period for Mughal Architecture.

questions.question: During their rule the British persuaded or forced cultivators in Bengal to grow _________.
questions.solution: The British persuaded and sometimes even forced cultivators in various parts of India to produce the crops of their choice. The crops that were forced on them were jute in Bengal, tea in Assam, sugarcane in Uttar Pradesh, wheat in Punjab, cotton in Maharashtra and Punjab, rice in Madras.

questions.question: The Mongols under _________ invaded Transoxiana in north-east Iran in 1219.
questions.solution:
The Mongols under **Genghis Khan** invaded Transoxiana in north-east Iran in 1219.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• The north-eastern part of Iran, Transoxiana was invaded by the Mongols under Genghis Khan in the year 1219.
 
• In this brief war, lasting less than two years, not only was a huge empire destroyed utterly, but Genghis Khan introduced the world to cruel tactics - indirect attack, and complete and utter terror and slaughter of populations wholesale as weapons of war.
 
• Soon after, the Mongols attacked the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.question: Metals react with sodium hydroxide to produce _________.
questions.solution:
Only the metals, whose oxides/hydroxides are amphoteric, react with strong water-soluble bases (Alkalies) to liberate Hydrogen gas. They are Be, Zn, Al, Sn, Pb, Cr, etc. & few metalloids (As, Sb, Ge) also.

Examples:

2Al + 2 NaOH + 2 H₂O → 2 NaAlO₂ + 3 H₂

Zn + 2 NaOH → Na₂ZnO₂ + H₂

questions.question: Presence of large amounts of nutrients in waters also causes excessive growth of _________ algae.
questions.solution: Favourable conditions for planktonic (blue-green) algae are stagnant water in combination with high temperature and high concentration of nutrients (like nitrogen). The lack of circulation of the water can cause the algae to over-compete other organisms in the ecosystem and thus create massive algae blooms.

questions.question: ________ means cases that can be directly considered by the Supreme Court without going to the lower courts before that.
questions.solution:
Option **1** is correct, i.e __**Original Jurisdiction**__.

__
 
• Supreme Court has** Original__ and Exclusive Jurisdiction** in Respect of Certain Disputes under Article 131, which means that **cases can be directly considered by the Supreme Court without going to the lower courts before that**.
 
• Its exclusive original jurisdiction extends to all cases between the Government of India and the States of India or between the Government of India and states on one side and one or more states on the other side or cases between different states.

Extra facts:

 
 

 
 
__Article__

 
 
 
__Statement__

 
 
 

 
 
Article131

 
 
 
States about the Orignal jurisdiction of the supreme court.

 
 
 

 
 
Article134A

 
 
 
States about the Certification for the appeal to the supreme court.

 
 
 

 
 
Article134

 
 
 
States about the Appellate jurisdiction of the supreme court in criminal matters.

 
 
 

 
 
Article133

 
 
 
States about the Appellate jurisdiction of the supreme court in an appeal from the high court in regards to civil matters.

 
 
 

 
 
Article132

 
 
 
States about the Appellate jurisdiction of the supreme court in an appeal from the high court in some cases.

 
 
 

 
 
Article135

 
 
 
States about the jurisdiction and power of the federal court under existing law to be exercisable by the supreme court.

 
 
 

 
 
Article136

 
 
 
States about the Special leave to appeal by the supreme court.

 
 
 

 
 
Article137

 
 
 
States about the Review of judgment by the supreme court.

 
 
 

 
 
Article128

 
 
 
States about the Attendance of retired Judges at sittings of the supreme court.

 
 
 

 
 
Article130

 
 
 
States about the Seat of Supreme Court.

questions.question: Which base is present in lime water?
questions.solution: Limewater is the common name for a diluted solution of calcium hydroxide. Limewater is prepared by stirring calcium hydroxide in pure water and filtering off the excess undissolved Ca(OH)₂. It is basic in nature.

questions.question: _________ is the relationship between the variable input and output, keeping all other inputs are held constant.
questions.solution: Suppose we vary a single input and keep all other inputs constant. Then for different levels of employment of that input, we get different levels of output from the production function. This relationship between the variable input and output, keeping all other inputs constant, is often referred to as Total Product(TP) of the variable input.

questions.question: Who invented the electric tram?
questions.solution: The world's first electric tram line operated in Sestroretsk near Saint Petersburg, Russia. It was invented and tested by Fyodor Pirotsky who was a Russian engineer of Ukrainian origin in 1880.

questions.solution: The 2015 Rugby World Cup Final was played between New Zealand and Australia on 31 October 2015 at Twickenham Stadium in London in which New Zealand defeated Australia. Dan Carter (New Zealand) was declared Man of the Match.

questions.solution: USA's ranked on the 10th position in 2016 Human Development Index published by the United Nations Development Programme. Its Human Development Index (HDI) value was 0.920.

questions.question: Under which of the following jurisdictions can any individual, whose fundamental right has been violated, can directly move the Supreme Court for the remedy?
questions.solution: If an individual’s fundamental rights are violated, then he/she can directly approach the High Court under Article 226 or Supreme Court under Article 32 of the Constitution of India. A *writ* is an order issued by an authority. Supreme court and High courts in India have the power to issue *writs* under article 32 and 226 respectively to enforce the fundamental rights.

questions.question: The closest example of a centrally planned economy is the _________ for the major part of the 20th Century.
questions.solution: The Soviet Union is the closest example of a centrally planned economy for the major part of the 20th Century. The economy of the Soviet Union was based on a system of state ownership of the means of production, collective farming, industrial manufacturing, and centralized administrative planning.

questions.question: Other name of Platelets is?
questions.solution: Platelets, also called thrombocytes are a component of blood whose function (along with the coagulation factors) is to stop bleeding by clumping and clotting blood vessel injuries.

questions.question: ___________ is the second largest animal phylum.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ **Mollusca.**__

**Explanation:**

 
• **Mollusca is the second-largest animal phylum**. They are terrestrial or aquatic.
 
• They exhibit an organ-system level of organization.
 
• They are **bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic, coelomate animals**. 
 
• They have an open circulatory system and kidney-like organs for excretion. The anterior head region has sensory tentacles.
 
• The mouth contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called a **radula**.
 
• They are usually dioecious and oviparous with indirect development.
 
• The body is covered by a calcareous shell and is unsegmented with a distinct head, muscular foot, and visceral hump. A soft and spongy layer of skin forms a mantle over the visceral hump.
 
• Examples are an **octopus, snails, and mussels.**

**About other Options:**

 
• **Chordata: **

 
 
• **​**Animals belonging to phylum Chordata is fundamentally characterized by the presence of a notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord, and paired pharyngeal gill slits.
 
• Phylum Chordata is divided into three subphyla:** Urochordata or Tunicata, Cephalochordata, and Vertebrata**. **Urochordata – Ascidia, Salpa, DoliolumCephalochordata – Amphioxus or Lancelet a**re examples of Chordata.
 
 
 
• **Annelida:**
 
 
• This phylum consists of segmented worms like Earthworms, leeches.
 
• They are triploblastic and coelomate with segmented body.
 
• They respire though their body surface and excrete through nephridia.
 
• They also have a well-developed circulatory and digestive system.

questions.question: In stems, the protoxylem lies towards the centre and the metaxylem lies towards the periphery of the organ. This type of primary xylem is called _________.
questions.solution: The development of primary xylem can be of four types namely, exarch, *endarch*, centrarch and mesarch. In vascular bundle, *endarch* is the arrangement where protoxylem (older xylem) is inside and metaxylem (newly formed) is outside. Development is inward to outward. Hence, protoxylem is found inside of metaxylem.

questions.question: Which of the following won the Best Film in 62nd Filmfare Awards 2017?
questions.solution: Filmfare Awards 2017 were held on January 14 at the NSCI Dome in Worli, Mumbai. The 62nd Jio Filmfare Awards was a star-studded event hosted by actor Shah Rukh Khan. Dangal won awards for Best film, director and actor.

questions.question: The time taken by a pendulum to complete one oscillation is called its?
questions.solution: One complete to and fro movement of the pendulum bob is called one vibration or one oscillation. The time taken by pendulum bob to complete one vibration or one oscillation is called the time period of the pendulum.

questions.question: The part of the Himalayas between Tista and Dihang rivers is known as _________ Himalayas.
questions.solution: The part of the Himalayas lying between the rivers Teesta and Dihang is known as Assam Himalayas, while the part of the Himalayas lying between the rivers Indus and Satluj is known as Punjab Himalayas, the part lying between the rivers Kali and Teesta is known as Nepal Himalayas and the part lying between the rivers Satluj and Kali is known as Kumaon Himalayas.

questions.question: The Delhi – Lahore Bus is officially known as _________.
questions.solution: The Delhi–Lahore Bus, officially known as Sada-e-Sarhad is a passenger bus service connecting the Indian capital of Delhi with the city of Lahore, Pakistan via the border transit post at Wagah.

questions.question: In the biosphere living beings are inter-related and interdependent on each other for survival. This life supporting system is known as the _________.
questions.solution: An ecosystem includes all of the living things (plants, animals and organisms) in a given area, interacting with each other, and also with their non-living environments (weather, earth, sun, soil, climate, atmosphere).

questions.question: In a qualitative way, the tendency of undisturbed objects to stay at rest or to keep moving with the same velocity is called _________.
questions.solution: Inertia is the name for the tendency of an object in motion to remain in motion, or an object at rest to remain at rest unless acted upon by a force. It is also defined as the tendency of objects to keep moving in a straight line at a constant velocity. The word inertia was first used by Johannes Kepler.

questions.question: What is the average of all numbers between 11 and 80 which are divisible by 6?
questions.solution:
First number to be divisible by 6 in this range = 12

Last number to be divisible by 6 in this range = 78

This is an AP with difference = 6

Let the total numbers in this AP be n

⇒ Average = Sum of AP/total numbers

⇒ Average = [n/2(last term + first term)]/n

⇒ Average = (last term + first term)/2

∴ Average = (12 + 78)/2 = 45

questions.question: The simple and compound interest that can be earned in two years at the same rate is Rs. 1500 and Rs. 1575 respectively. What is the rate (% per annum) of interest?
questions.solution:
Let P be the Principal and R be the rate of interest

SI = (P × R × T)/100 = 1500

⇒ PR = 150000/2

⇒ PR = 75000

⇒ P = 75000/R

CI = P(1 + R/100n)ⁿt - P = P(1 + R/100)² - P = 1575

⇒ P(1 + R/100)² - P = 1575

⇒ 75000/R(1 + R/50 + R²/10000) -75000/R = 1575

⇒ 1500R + 7.5R² = 1575R

Dividing by 7.5

⇒ R² - 10R = 0

⇒ R(R -10) = 0

∴ R = 10 as R can’t be 0

questions.solution:

questions.question: Sum of four times a fraction and 6 times its reciprocal is 11. What is the fraction?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sum of four times a fraction and 6 times its reciprocal is 11.

**Calculations:**

Let the fraction be a

So, 4a + 6/a = 11

⇒ 4a² - 11a + 6 = 0

⇒ 4a² - 8a - 3a + 6 = 0

⇒ 4a(a - 2) - 3(a - 2) = 0

⇒ (4a - 3)(a - 2) = 0

∴ a = 3/4 and 2

Centroid of a Triangle is the intersection of all the medians

⇒ x - coordinate = (x₁ + x₂ + x₃)/3 = (1 + 4 -2)/3 = 1

⇒ y - coordinate = (y₁ + y₂ + y₃)/3 = (-5 + 0 + 2)/3 = -1

So, (x, y) = (1, -1)

questions.question: What is the reflection of the point (5, 2) in the line x = -3?
questions.solution:
To find: reflection of the point (5, 2) in the line x = -3

⇒ the equation of line is: x + 3 = 0

The formula for finding the image of a point (x₁, y₁) to the line ax + by + c = 0 is given by:

(x - x₁)/a = (y - y₁)/b = -2(ax₁ + by₁ + c)/(a² + b²)

Here, a = 1, b = 0 and c = 3

So, we have

(x - 5)/(1) = - 2(5 + 3)/(1) and (y - 2) = 0

⇒ x - 5 = -16 and y = 2

∴ x = -11

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a4e982a5fcfb52688b20873ba6cf25c43fb2d0d0a53c55a21d12a132ad4029ad.png] 

The distance of line x = -3 from the reflection will be the same as the distance from the original point.

Distance of x- coordinate of line from the original point = 5 + 3 = 8

The distance of x- coordinate of the line from the reflected point 

= - 3 - 8 = -11 ( As it is on the other side of the axis)

The y- coordinate is constant in the line x = -3, therefore y- coordinate will be remain the same.

The refection point = (-11, 2)

∴ x = 1

 Let AP be 2b. Then, AR will be 7b
